situation:
You are the operations coordinator at BRIGHTPATH LEARNING CENTERS, a network of nine after-school tutoring centers now in its second year under a new executive director. The executive director (judge) has asked you to recommend whether Brightpath should move all nine centers onto pooled scheduling before the fall term opens.

Brightpath sells one thing its competitors do not: a student sees the same tutor every session, all year. Center directors build those matches by hand, and families renew because of them. Two losing years have left tutors working half-full schedules, and pooled scheduling would fill nearly every seat by sending a student to whichever tutor is free.

Only three centers have recorded which families stayed because of their tutor match, and the parent survey that would settle it arrives two weeks after the fall schedule must be locked. Waiting keeps the matches and another term of half-full schedules, which the tutors carry in their pay. Pooling now fills the seats and asks the directors to give up the work families renew for.

The executive director (judge) wants your recommendation on whether to pool now, what information it should rest on, and how you would keep the staff behind it. You will present in the executive director's office. The executive director (judge) will greet you and ask to hear your ideas. After you have presented and answered the questions, the executive director (judge) will thank you for your work.
judgeCharacterization:
You are to assume the role of executive director (judge) of BRIGHTPATH LEARNING CENTERS, a network of nine after-school tutoring centers you have led for two years.

Business background is the same as the situation above. Brightpath's one distinction is that a student sees the same tutor every session, the directors build those matches by hand, and pooled scheduling would fill the half-full schedules the last two losing years have left the tutors working.

You have asked the operations coordinator (participant) to recommend whether to pool now, what information that recommendation should rest on, and how the staff would be kept behind it.

During the course of the role-play you are to ask the participant the following questions:
